messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: showing part of output
parts:
So, I'm curious, I'm trying to make slides of output from lme objects in beamer slides, but there is a LOT in the summary.  I want to walk through it piece by piece.  While one can feed arguments to echo to only show part of the entered code, is there a similar way to manipulate, say, include?

Thanks!

-Jarrett

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] showing part of output
parts:
I would recommend you to use \begin{frame}[fragile,allowframebreaks]
in this case.

If you want to tweak the output, here is an example of truncating long output:

https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/052-suppress-output.md
https://github.com/yihui/knitr-examples/blob/master/052-suppress-output.Rmd

I guess it should not be too hard to modify it to write specified
lines of the chunk output.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] showing part of output
parts:
Hmm... that is yet another problem of the framed package.

Both render_listings() and render_sweave() work in this case; the
default style does not allow frame breaks.

Regards,

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] showing part of output
parts:
It is probably not because it does not work for summary objects. Line
15 has modified x, so what is x in line 18?

I think you can use this: x[intersect(seq_along(x), seq(n[1], n[2]))]

I would rather make out.lines a vector of indices of elements you want
to keep instead of the starting and ending lines, so that
x[intersect(seq_along(x), n)] will be what you want, e.g.
out.lines=5:10

Regards,
Yihui
